subject: arcadeCabinet
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: 1980s arcade cabinet.
Style: synthwave.

spec.name: Neon Rush Arcade Cabinet
spec.description: A 1980s upright arcade cabinet in synthwave style: near-black purple carcass with neon T-molding, side art of a striped sunset sun, perspective grid and palms, a glowing marquee, a CRT showing a neon-horizon racer, and an angled two-player control deck.
spec.layout: Static prop, no joints. Real 1980s upright size, about 1.86 m tall. It is centred on x=0 and +Z is the player side. The side-panel silhouette (z,y), clockwise from the back foot, is (-0.44,0.04) (0.40,0.04) (0.40,0.84) (0.46,0.84) (0.46,0.96) (0.22,1.08) (0.22,1.52) (0.245,1.52) (0.245,1.86) (-0.30,1.86) (-0.44,1.72). Side panels are 0.025 thick, occupying x 0.325..0.35 and -0.35..-0.325. From front to back, bottom to top: (1) a kickplate (y 0.04-0.20) and a lower front wall at z=0.40 (y 0.04-0.84) carrying the coin door. (2) The control deck, a plate sloping from front edge (z 0.46, y 0.96) up to back edge (z 0.22, y 1.08), about 26.6 degrees, with surface normal about [0,0.894,0.447]. It overhangs the lower front by 0.06, with a front apron y 0.84-0.96 at z=0.46. (3) The monitor bezel, y 1.08-1.52, leaning back about 5 degrees, bottom edge at z=0.22 and top edge at z=0.19, with the glowing CRT inset. (4) The marquee box, y 1.52-1.86, z -0.415..0.245, which overhangs the bezel by 0.025 and carries a glowing title panel on its front face. (5) A flat back panel at z=-0.44..-0.415. SYNTHWAVE STYLE: the carcass is deep purple-black with no wood tone. Every edge, the deck lip, the marquee border and the screen frame are outlined by thin neon strips (cyan, hot pink and yellow). The colour order is always pink to orange to yellow in the sun and cyan to violet in the grid. Side art is a sunset sun cut by horizontal slits, a perspective grid floor, jagged mountain triangles, palm silhouettes and stars, all built from thin extruded or box parts seated on the outer side faces (x = ±0.352 to ±0.360), mirrored identically on both sides with the sun at z=-0.05. Neon, screen, marquee, buttons and underglow use the glow kit (flat colours only). All detail is built from small flat-colour parts: no paints or textures are required, though text may use svg textures on thin planes. Keep the facets low-poly and chunky: rounded joystick balls and buttons use 8-10 segments.

parts.builds: The structural cabinet shell in cabBlack/cabPurple. It has two extruded side panels from the stated silhouette (x 0.325..0.35, mirrored; cabBlack, with a 0.006 cabPurple bevel inset border on the outer face). It also has the back panel (z -0.44..-0.415, y 0.04..1.86) with a recessed vent grille of dark slats and a screwed access door outline, a floor base slab (y 0.04..0.10) and four chunky levelling feet in steel (y 0..0.04, with chrome nut rings). It also has the lower front wall (z 0.375..0.40, x +-0.325, y 0.04..0.84), the kickplate (y 0.04..0.20, set 0.01 back) with a neon cyan strip along its top edge, and a deck support shelf under the control deck. The neon T-molding is thin glowing strips (0.008 square) following the side panel edges on both sides: neonCyan on the front and top edges, neonPink on the back and bottom edges, and a neonYellow accent along the deck step. A power cord with a plug, an on/off switch and a small panel screw head set sit on the back. Hidden sides are fine to leave simple. Nothing blocks the deck, bezel, marquee or coin door areas.
parts.attaches: Side panels carry the deck, bezel and marquee edges at the profile points (deckFrontEdge, deckBackEdge, bezelBottom, marqueeBottom). The lowerFront wall is where coinDoor part sits. The sideFaceL/R mounts are the outer faces for sideArt.

parts.builds: The synthwave side-panel art on the outer faces (x from 0.352 to 0.360 on +X, mirrored on -X), built entirely from thin parts in different colours. It has a full-panel gradient of horizontal bands from cabBlack at the bottom through panelIndigo and deepViolet to horizonViolet near the horizon at y about 0.95, as stacked thin extruded strips following the side silhouette. A giant sun (disc, radius about 0.26, centre z=-0.05, y=1.05) with a vertical gradient from sunMagenta to sunOrange to neonYellow, built as 4-5 stacked disc slices cut by growing horizontal slit gaps toward the bottom. A perspective grid floor below the horizon in gridMagenta and neonCyan: radiating lines converging at the sun, plus horizontal lines that get closer together toward the horizon. Two or three layered jagged mountain ridges silhouetted in voidBlack with thin neonCyan edge outlines. Two palm trees in voidBlack (trunk and fan of 5-6 pointed fronds) near the front lower area. About 25 small neonWhite and neonPink star diamonds in the upper region. A thin neonPink and neonCyan racing double stripe running along the lower edge. All parts stay inside the side silhouette, clear of the cabinet's edge T-molding (keep 0.02 margin), and stay on the outer face only.
parts.attaches: Sits on sideFaceL (x=+0.35) and sideFaceR (x=-0.35), 2 to 10 mm proud of the carcass side panels.

parts.builds: The angled control deck between the side panels (x +-0.325), from deckFrontEdge to deckBackEdge. It has a 0.03 thick sloped plate in panelIndigo, a front apron (y 0.84..0.96, z 0.43..0.46, cabBlack with a glowing neonPink lip strip along its top and a neonCyan strip along its bottom), and an underside wedge. The overlay is a thin voidBlack control plate on the deck surface with neonPink and neonCyan angled stripe graphics and small white 'P1' / 'P2' / 'START' marks as thin parts. There are two joysticks (P1 at joystickP1, P2 at joystickP2): a chrome round base plate with steel dust cover, a thin steel shaft and a chunky ball top (one neonRed buttonRed, one buttonBlue), each a bit tilted never. Each side has three glowing arcade buttons (buttonRed, neonYellow, buttonGreen/buttonBlue for P2) at x about +-0.05, +-0.10, +-0.15, z staggered 0.33-0.39, each with a dark ring, round cap and a small white highlight. Two lit start buttons (neonCyan, neonPink) sit at startButtons, x +-0.04. There is a small brassCoin-coloured coin return and a chrome speaker or logo medallion in the back-centre of the deck, plus bolt heads at the plate corners. Controls stand perpendicular to the deck normal (deckNormal).
parts.attaches: Plate edges meet the side panels' sloped profile at deckFrontEdge and deckBackEdge. The back of the deck meets the monitor head at bezelBottom (z=0.22, y=1.08). The front apron sits above the coinDoor part at y=0.84.

parts.builds: Everything from the bezel up. It has the bezel, a bezelBlack frame y 1.08..1.52 across x +-0.325, leaning back about 5 degrees, with angled neonCyan and neonPink corner slashes on it. The CRT screen is 0.50 wide x 0.34 high, centred at screenCentre and slightly inset, with a rounded dark glass bulge (screenDark), a glowing display built in layers (glow kit): a screenGlow sky gradient in stacked bands, a sunMagenta/sunOrange striped sun, horizonViolet mountains, a neonCyan/gridMagenta perspective grid road, and a tiny racing car with two glowing red taillights. It also has a HUD in neonYellow/neonCyan thin parts ('SCORE', 'HI', digits, 'LIVES' icons). A thin white glare streak sits on the glass corner and the screen has a thin neonCyan outline. The marquee box (y 1.52..1.86, x +-0.325, z -0.415..0.245) is cabBlack with a front marquee panel (glowing, panelIndigo base) carrying the title 'NEON RUSH' in big neonPink block letters with neonCyan outline offset (letter shapes from thin box parts or a thin svg text plane), a neonYellow sun-and-grid emblem on each side of it, and small neon chaser dots along the border. A glowing neonPink and neonCyan double border tube frames the marquee front. A top cap (y 1.84..1.86) covers the head, with a neonYellow strip along the front-top edge. Speaker grille slits sit in dark horizontal bars under the marquee on both sides of the bezel top.
parts.attaches: Bezel bottom edge is at bezelBottom (z 0.22, y 1.08), meeting the deck's back edge. The marquee box bottom rests on the bezel top at marqueeBottom (y 1.52). Its sides are flush with the carcass side panels, and the back is flush with the carcass back panel at z=-0.415.

parts.builds: The lower-front hardware on the lowerFront wall (z 0.40, y 0.20..0.84), built outward to z 0.43. It has a chrome-framed coin door plate (about 0.28 wide x 0.36 high, voidBlack plate, steel frame, four chrome corner screws, a recessed lock with a brassCoin face and keyhole). There are two coin mechs (left and right) with a chrome slot face, a glowing buttonRed 'INSERT COIN' lit insert-coin light bar, a coin return flap with a dark opening, and a tiny CREDIT counter in neonYellow digits. Above it is a glowing neonCyan 'INSERT COIN' strip with neonPink arrows on a cabBlack plate. Two side speaker/vent grille panels (dark slats) sit left and right of the door. A neon underglow strip (neonPink, 0.01 thick) runs across the front at y 0.21 over the kickplate with a neonCyan twin below it, plus a tiny sticker of a pink sun-and-grid emblem and chrome handle pulls on the lower front. Nothing extends into the deck's apron above y 0.84.
parts.attaches: Back faces meet the carcass lower front wall at z=0.40 (mount lowerFront / coinDoorCentre). The top edge ends at y=0.84 below the deck apron. The underglow strip lies above the carcass kickplate at y 0.20.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching a spec for a synthwave 1980s arcade cabinet as a static model with no joints, sized at roughly 0.76 wide, 1.85 tall, and 0.95 deep to account for the control panel overhang and marquee, facing +Z.

I'm splitting the cabinet into parts: a carcass with the side profiles, base, back, and neon trim; a separate sideArt part for the synthwave graphics on both sides; a controlDeck with the angled panel and controls; and a screenAssembly covering the bezel, the glowing screen, and the lit marquee.

I'm settling the cabinet's side panels at 0.025 thickness, with the overall width set at 0.70, and I'm sketching the side profile in the z-y plane to define the base and upper body shape.

I'm working out the side panel profile now, settling the z range at -0.44 to 0.46 so the overall depth comes to 0.90, and starting the outline at a small lift off the floor.

I'm working out the side profile's upper edge now: the lower front sits at z 0.40, rising to about y 0.84, then the control deck pushes forward to z 0.46 and slopes back up toward the screen, which tilts back from around y 1.06.

I'm settling the side profile's outline now: it runs along the lower front, steps forward for the control deck, then rises back toward the screen and the marquee, with the top tapering in as it goes.

I'm reconsidering the top of the side profile: the back corner could get a chamfer, running from around y 1.70 at the back to the full height near the front. I'm also wondering whether the profile should step back between the control deck and the marquee, since the screen opening sits there.

I'm settling the screen bezel as a black frame tilted slightly back, spanning between the sides, with the glass inset behind it, and I'm adding mounts for the monitor.

Still writing the color palette...

I'm listing the palette entries and then working out the mount points: the floor base at the origin, the left side-art mount on the outer face, and the control deck's front and back edges. I'm also computing the deck's slope, roughly 27 degrees from horizontal, and its surface normal for the control panel.

I'm placing the deck's mount points and computing its slope normal, then marking the screen center, the bezel edges with a slight back tilt, and the marquee's front face.

I'm laying out the carcass's front panel as a solid piece spanning most of the width, with the kickplate and back panel finishing the box.

I'm laying out how the control deck gets supported: a sloped box spanning between the side panels, with a front apron below it. The deck will carry the joysticks, buttons, and trackball, along with its neon strip and decals.

I'm laying out the monitor head as a box spanning the cabinet's width, with the bezel and synthwave screen scene at its front, and I'm working through the marquee, which sits above it with a neon tube trim.

I'm settling the monitor head as one part spanning the full width, with the bezel, screen, marquee box with its neon trim, and a top cap at the top, all sitting between the side panels.

I'm grouping the lower front details into a coinDoor part, with the coin door plate, coin slots, glowing return buttons, the "INSERT COIN" strip, and a neon underglow along the base. I'm also checking whether that leaves enough detail to cover the remaining surfaces of the cabinet.

I'm checking the budget against the parts list: carcass 150, side art 220, control deck 200, monitor head 220, and coin door 100, which totals 890 and fits under 900. For the side panels, I'm placing the art on the outer faces with a gradient background, a sun cut with horizontal slits, perspective horizon lines, mountains, palms, and stars, all within the z range -0.40 to 0.20 and the height band from 0.2 to 1.8.

I'm working out how the side art reads from outside each cabinet side, placing the lower gradient bands and the sun disc within the profile's z and y ranges, and checking which way the mirrored panels face when viewed from each side.

I'm checking the side-art orientation: from each side, the front of the cabinet appears on opposite sides of the view, so the mirrored panels need to keep the sun at the same z position on both. I'm also setting the layout fields, with no joints and two side-face mount points, and starting to lay out the overall bounds.

I'm checking the deck's width and depth: the z range now runs to 0.48 with the lip, the overall size comes to 0.70 by 1.86 by 0.92, and the joysticks clear the top with room to spare.

I'm settling the control deck's panel as a slope running from the front lip down toward the back, and I'm placing the joysticks at roughly x ±0.19 with the buttons clustered beside each one.

I'm placing the two joysticks out toward the outer edges of the deck, with the start buttons sitting near the center between them.

I'm working out the joystick and button placement on the control deck: the joysticks sit toward the outer edges, with three buttons per player stepping inward from each stick.

I'm placing the two joysticks at matching points on the deck, roughly 0.24 out from center and near z 0.35, and working out the surface height there from the slope. I'm also putting the start buttons near the back center of the deck and placing the marquee's face mount above the monitor head.

I'm checking the marquee's height and the bezel's placement: the marquee runs from about y 1.52 to 1.86, and the bezel spans y 1.08 to 1.52. I'm sketching the side profile's step at the top to match, with the marquee face sitting slightly forward of the bezel.

I'm settling the screen content as a synthwave scene with a sun and perspective grid, plus a racing view with car taillights, and the bezel gets angled pink and cyan stripes on its sides. I'm sizing the screen at about 0.50 by 0.34, centered around y 1.30, and starting to write the JSON.

I'm putting the carcass box at full width and height, with the feet at the base, and noting that the carcass overlaps the monitor head's top cap. Overlapping boxes are fine as long as they share faces, so I'll state that in the spec.
